test_title: SSC MTS Previous Year Paper (Held on: 26 July 2022 Shift 1)
subject: general
question: S₁ and S₂ can do a piece of work together in 18 days, S₂ and S₃ can do the same work together in 27 days, while S₃ and S₁ can do it together in 54 days. In how many days can all 3, working together, do 50% of the work?
solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

Combined efficiency of 2(S₁ + S₂ + S₃) = (Total Work ÷ 18) + (Total Work ÷ 27) + (Total Work ÷ 54).

LCM of 18, 27, 54 = 54. Efficiencies: (S₁+S₂)=3, (S₂+S₃)=2, (S₃+S₁)=1.

Sum of efficiencies = 3 + 2 + 1 = 6 ⇒ Efficiency of (S₁+S₂+S₃) = 6 ÷ 2 = 3.

50% of work = 54 × 0.5 = 27 units. Time = 27 ÷ 3 = 9 days.

**∴ The correct answer is 9 days.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:** Time for (S₁ + S₂) = 18 days, (S₂ + S₃) = 27 days, (S₃ + S₁) = 54 days.

**Formula Used:** Total Work = LCM of individual days; Efficiency = Total Work ÷ Time.

⇒ Adding all efficiencies: 2 × (S₁ + S₂ + S₃) = 3 + 2 + 1 = 6

⇒ Efficiency of (S₁ + S₂ + S₃) = 6 ÷ 2 = 3 units/day

⇒ 50% of Total Work = 54 ÷ 2 = 27 units

⇒ Time taken by all three = 27 ÷ 3 = 9 days

**∴ The correct answer is 9 days.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Combined Work Principle

When workers work in pairs, the sum of their efficiencies represents twice the total efficiency of the group. Total Efficiency = (Sum of pair efficiencies) ÷ 2.

Work Percentage

To find time for a fraction of work, multiply the Total Work by the percentage (e.g., 50% = 0.5) before dividing by efficiency.</p
